t.E1442.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E1442.body: Modified starches are not absorbed intact; in the gut they are largely broken down by enzymes, and the remainder is fermented by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E1442.prod: Produced by modifying starch through a chemical reaction (modified starch).
t.E1442.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E1442.summary: Modified starch: maize, potato or wheat starch that has been chemically or physically treated to make it resistant to heat, acid and freezing. It adds thickness to sauces, soups, ready-made desserts and yoghurts.
t.E1442.what: Cross-linked hydroxypropyl starch; it provides a thickness that is resistant to heat, acid and freezing.
